summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator Cas Russell parts ways with Tresting in a rundown neighborhood after they escape pursuers, including Pithica and the police. Russell feels awkward about the goodbye and reflects with some irritation that he has started to care about Arthur, whom he compares unfavorably to Dawna Polk's social skill. Afterward Russell walks, takes the metro to Union Station, and buys a disguise of an "I ♥ LA" shirt, cap, sunglasses and tote bag.
one_line: Cas Russell parts ways with Tresting, reflects on caring about Arthur, and disguises himself at Union Station in Los Angeles.
key_facts: Tresting tells the narrator he will be fine after the narrator reminds him that Pithica is after him, along with the police and other men.
The narrator parks the van in the seediest-looking neighborhood he can find and both get out.
Tresting thanks the narrator for saving his life back at his office, and the narrator replies "We're even."
Tresting tells the narrator, "You ain't gotta be like this," urging him to change.
The narrator replies "I like how I am just fine" before Tresting walks away.
The narrator reflects that Dawna Polk has a superpowered human relations ability that would have helped her connect with Arthur.
The narrator admits that he has started to care about Arthur, whether he lives or dies and what he thinks.
The narrator decides the solution is to stop caring about Arthur and to never make that mistake again.
The narrator walks for a while and then takes the metro, which he had tended to forget Los Angeles had.
The narrator rides the metro line up to Union Station.
At a tourist stand in Union Station, the narrator buys a large "I ♥ LA" T-shirt, a baseball cap, sunglasses, and a tote bag.
The sunglasses cover half the narrator's face, including most of the bruising.
